images.alt: The front panel of a BeBox, a beige tower with a row of red LED lights above the drive bays
images.caption: The BeBox (1995), Be Inc.'s dual-PowerPC workstation — the LED row across the front, nicknamed the 'Blinkenlights,' showed CPU load per core in real time.

images.alt: An early prototype BeBox tower, beige case with a rounded top and front LED array, photographed at an angle
images.caption: An early BeBox prototype, before the design was finalized for production in 1995.

images.alt: A production BeBox tower sitting on a desk next to a monitor and keyboard, in use
images.caption: A production BeBox on a desk. Fewer than 2,000 units were built before Be shifted BeOS to standard PowerPC Macs and then x86 PCs.

images.alt: An expansion board removed from a production BeBox, showing chips and connectors
images.caption: An expansion board from inside a BeBox. Alongside standard PCI slots, the machine exposed a proprietary 'GeekPort' for driving external electronics directly from software.
Jean-Louis Gassée, former Apple executive who co-founded Be Inc. in 1990 and led it through the BeBox, BeOS, and the 2001 sale to Palm.

images.alt: A close-up of a metal identification plate on a production BeBox, showing its serial number
images.caption: A production BeBox's serial tag. Be Inc. stopped selling its own hardware in 1997 and refocused on licensing BeOS for standard PowerPC Macs and PCs.
